A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EchoGen research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are sufficiently readable to match retained material and identify additions and revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original DreamBench evaluations, a human preference study, component ablations, guidance experiments, and generated-image comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds latency experiments, segmentation robustness tests, further ablations, and evaluations under two reference-scoring protocols.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the Infinity backbone, DINOv2 semantic injection, FLUX VAE content injection, attention masks, frozen parameters, and subject-text guidance rule. The added discussion of optional Qwen2.5-VL use provides implementation clarification; it does not establish a redesigned algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 substantially expands training-data coverage by adding filtered UNO-1M single-object data, generated using an Object-365 taxonomy, to Subjects200K. It also evaluates imperfect-localization scenarios with shifted and enlarged bounding boxes. DreamBench and DreamBench++ remain the evaluation benchmarks; real-world subject generation was already represented in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds the Infinity-2B-based AR-Booth comparator and removes BootPIG. The other main comparators and human-study methods remain. The new protocol and latency experiments reuse IP-Adapter, OminiControl, and EasyControl.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported training corpus from approximately 256,000 to 640,000 triplets and the schedule from 20 epochs to 80K iterations. Added experiments vary diffusion denoising steps, compare single- and multi-reference scoring using common evaluation code, and apply 10% bounding-box perturbations. However, v2's appendix and Table 9 retain 20 epochs, leaving the exact revised training budget unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds denoising-step sensitivity and component-latency analyses, a qualitative semantic/content ablation, semantic-versus-content prefix tests, segmentation-perturbation robustness, scoring-protocol comparisons, and illustrated failure cases. These substantially broaden the diagnostic evidence in Sections 5.2, 5.3, 7.4, and 7.6. The existing classifier-free-guidance sweep is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, dispersion estimates, or statistical significance tests. The human study retains 25 participants, 450 responses, and preference ratios; the added quantitative displays also report point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces EchoGen-2B's DINO/CLIP-I/CLIP-T values of 0.686/0.807/0.324 with 0.755/0.835/0.325 and changes EasyControl's reported latency from 47.6s to 25.4s. Encoder and segmentation ablation values also change. New latency, robustness, prefix, protocol, and qualitative results substantially expand the evidence, while human preferences remain unchanged. Changed training and inconsistent reference-scoring labels prevent interpreting the larger scores as a controlled same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same autoregressive factorization, attention operations, and guidance formulation. No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: the first feed-forward VAR-based subject-driven framework, dual semantic/content injection, and competitive generation quality with substantially lower latency. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning latency bottlenecks, robustness to imperfect segmentation, and synthetic-to-real transfer. Section 7.6 identifies limited DINOv2 input resolution as an additional source of detail/text failures. It retains backbone limitations but removes v1's prediction that Subjects200K would become insufficient for larger models.

D1.justification: The abstract changes a promised future code/model release into a reported public release with a repository address. v2 also documents UNO-1M subset selection, filtering and access, H20 timing hardware, evaluator expertise, explicit reference-scoring conventions, and optional subject descriptions that bypass Qwen2.5-VL. These materially expand reproducibility information, although the training-schedule inconsistency remains.

R1.justification: The BootPIG citation and bibliography entry are removed. AR-Booth becomes an explicit experimental comparator, but its underlying Chung et al. work was already cited; Wu et al., now also supporting UNO-1M usage, was likewise present. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most introductory, methodological, and related-work prose is retained. Local wording changes, revised affiliation/contact information, and expanded dataset and experiment explanations accompany the additions. The appendix gains an analysis subsection, and the former standalone limitations section becomes Section 7.6; there is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds latency plots, a qualitative component ablation, real-world examples, and failure panels in Figures 5, 6, 9, and 10, plus timing, prefix, robustness, and two-protocol tables. These substantially expand the visual presentation. Existing architecture diagrams and comparison images are retained; the original guidance plot and appendix comparison become Figures 7 and 8.

improvement.justification: The denoising-budget comparisons and component timings better support the central efficiency argument, while robustness tests, failure examples, and reported code/model access improve scrutiny and reproducibility. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Section 5.1 specifies 80K iterations while the appendix retains 20 epochs, and EchoGen-2B's Table 1 scores match Table 12(a)'s multi-reference row despite the stated single-reference protocol. The added diagnostic evidence supports a limited overall improvement, but the numerical increases do not establish a controlled performance gain.
